audit.whatIsWrong: This page's chart (Skill, Gnar, Gnar, Skill, Skill, Gnar, Gnar) disagrees with the Cho'Gath-side mirror, which was already set to Gnar, Gnar, Skill, Skill, Cho'Gath, Cho'Gath, Skill — and with its own whys, which give Gnar level 1, call level 3 'genuinely even', and concede 6 and first item to Cho'Gath.
audit.why: Cho'Gath has no dash, so levels 1-2 are Gnar's; from 6 Feast (80/70/60s) is flat true damage that chunks or executes a Mini body; his tank-item spike out-bulks form-dependent burst.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Gnar, Gnar, Skill, Skill, Cho'Gath, Cho'Gath, Skill — identical to the mirror and the packet chart, so mirror-fix.js has nothing to overwrite.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page tracked Feast as the matchup-defining cooldown but never gave its number, and never gave Feral Scream's.
audit.why: Feast is 80/70/60s and GNAR! is 90/60/30s, so early on his ultimate is available more often than yours — that is the actual reason to hold Rage rather than spend it. Feral Scream is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s.
audit.corrected: Both numbers written into the cooldown block, the do's and the level-6 phase why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer stated the two interactions that decide the trade: Hop clears Rupture's delayed knockup, and Feral Scream's silence removes Hop and the transform.
audit.why: Rupture ruptures the ground at a location after a delay, so a 475-range leap taken on the tell avoids it. Feral Scream silences, and a silenced Gnar cannot cast Hop or press an ability to complete the Rage transform — which is why his combo order is scream first, then Rupture. The mirror states the same interaction from his side (catch him mid-Hop, silence, then Feast).
audit.corrected: Written into the cooldown block, the do's, the don'ts and the interactions report.

audit.why: Cho'Gath's kit file flags Rupture as 'grounding', but Riot's description says it pops enemies into the air. Per the calibration rule I trusted the description and treated it as a knockup everywhere — the mirror did the same.
audit.corrected: No grounding claim written; the page keeps calling it a knockup.

edits.before: Boomerang + hop kite wins every melee matchup early. Identify how Cho'Gath contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: He has no dash to close, so Mini autos plus a Boomerang win the first trade at 1 — Rupture's knockup is still a level away.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Cho'Gath must walk into your range.
edits.after: Full kits online, but so is Rupture into Feral Scream — trade only when Rage lines up for a Mega answer.

edits.before: Mega + R against a wall is the best engage top lane owns. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Cho'Gath's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Feast lands at 6: one cast chunks a third of Mini's HP or executes you outright, and at 80s it is up more often than GNAR!.

edits.before: Stridebreaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Feast's cooldown.
edits.after: His HP and tank items out-bulk your form burst — refuse the all-in on Rage downtime.

edits.before: - Cho'Gath Feast: matchup-defining — True-damage execute. Don’t sit low. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Cho'Gath Feast (80s at rank 1): matchup-defining — flat true damage, so resistances do not help. Don't sit low. - Feral Scream (11s) silences: silenced, you cannot Hop or transform. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

edits.before: True-damage execute. Don’t sit low. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Flat true damage, 80s at rank 1. Only engage once it is down or baited.

edits.before: Cho'Gath wastes Feast — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Hop clears Rupture's delayed knockup — poke, then leap out.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Feral Scream silences: no Hop, no transform, no escape from Rupture.

edits.before: Track Cho'Gath's Feast: True-damage execute. Don’t sit low. When it is down — Boomerang-W + R him.
edits.after: Hop clears Rupture's delayed knockup, but Feral Scream's silence turns Hop off. Feast is flat true damage.

notes: Chart flips are one atomic group across both layers and are copied from the Cho'Gath-side mirror, so the two directions now agree. Rupture is written as a knockup, not grounding: the kit's grounding flag contradicts Riot's own description and the mirror treated it the same way. The Feast-versus-GNAR! cooldown comparison (80s against 90s at rank 1) is the concrete reason the page's 'hold your ultimate' advice is right, and it was missing.
